output.summary: Two signature changes, each with its own callers: formatPrice in src/price.ts gains a currency parameter and tax in tax.py gains a rate parameter (default 0.1). The TypeScript callers pass 'USD' and the Python callers pass 0.2, so the two roots are independent. Four edits look unrelated to either root: the config currency switches to EUR, the legacy label text changes, viaMethod's argument changes, and use_calc's argument changes. Check that the hard-coded 'USD' callers still agree with the EUR default in config.json.

groups.title: formatPrice gains a currency parameter
groups.description: The definition now takes a currency and returns it as a prefix. Read it first. Check that the output format change is intended.

groups.title: Callers pass 'USD' to formatPrice
groups.description: checkoutSummary, invoiceSummary and receiptSummary each pass 'USD', and aliasCaller calls it through the fmt re-export. Check that none should pass another currency, and that 'USD' agrees with the config default.

groups.title: tax gains an optional rate parameter
groups.description: tax now takes a rate, defaulting to 0.1, and multiplies by it. Existing one-argument calls keep their behaviour. Check the default is intended.

groups.title: order_total and refund pass a 0.2 rate
groups.description: order_total calls tax directly and refund calls it through the t alias. Both now pass 0.2, which differs from the 0.1 default. Check that 0.2 is the intended rate for both.

groups.title: Other edits that look unrelated to the two signature changes
groups.description: config.json switches the currency to EUR, legacyLabel changes its text to 'Old', and viaMethod and use_calc change literal arguments. None of these calls the changed tax or formatPrice: the fmt and calc calls resolve to methods, and legacyLabel uses a different formatPrice in legacy/price.ts. Confirm each is intended on its own.

edgeVerdicts.reason: viaMethod's parameter f is typed Fmt, so f.formatPrice is the Fmt.formatPrice method, not the standalone formatPrice function in price.ts.
Calc().tax(2) calls the Calc.tax method defined in calc.py, not the module-level tax function in tax.py.
